turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Sorry, the car park's been a nightmare, I could see the queue from the window. I'll just do your observations before you're called.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning. Thank you. We did find a space eventually. I apologise if we have kept you waiting.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We weren't late. We were sat in the corridor. Uh, the ticket machine ate my card. Twice.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Happens all the time. Right. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Your last pressure was one-forty.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): I see. I was rather wound up at that appointment, if I recall correctly.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Mm. Pulse seventy-two. Weight fifty-two kilograms. Last time in March you were sixty-eight. Temperature thirty-eight point three.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sixty-eight? That's a drop. And, umm, thirty-eight point three, that sounds high.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): The weight was intentional. I changed my diet after March, and I am not concerned about it.
[SEG0009] person_1 (NURSE): That's what the thermometer reads, thirty-eight point three, so I'll chart it. Doctor won't be long.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello. Come through, both of you, that's quite all right. What brings you in today?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you for seeing me. I have come about a pain in my jaw when I chew. It has become rather troublesome.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pain on chewing. Um, how long has it been, and where exactly do you feel it?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, about three weeks. Well, actually it has been three weeks. It is an ache just in front of the ear, and the jaw clicks when I open. It is worse when I am stressed.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He grinds his teeth as well. I hear it at night, most nights, for two or three weeks. He only half believes me.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I do believe you. I simply was not aware of the grinding until it was pointed out. I am sorry it disturbs you.

[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. Pain with chewing, a click, grinding at night. I'm thinking this sits in the jaw joint rather than a tooth, err, the grinding loads the joint and the stress clamps the muscle. Does that match what you feel?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that is a fair description. I have had no trouble with the teeth themselves.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any fever? Have you felt properly unwell? Any swelling you've noticed?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I have not had a fever, I have not felt unwell, and I have not noticed any swelling.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Does it lock at all, or is it only the click? Any earache, or a change in your hearing?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): It does not lock. I can open fully, it merely clicks. No earache, and my hearing is normal.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): And your chest, just briefly. Any cough, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing of that kind. My breathing is perfectly fine.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): What are you taking for it? Any regular medicines?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Only paracetemol. One gram, um, four times a day, for the past week, for the jaw. I take nothing else regularly.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His sister keeps on about biotin. She takes high strength biotin herself, for her hair, and she wants him on it. I said no.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I have not taken her biotin, and I would not start it without your advice.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Quite right, that's hers, not yours, and it won't touch a jaw joint. Any allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I have no allergies that I am aware of.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me feel the joint. Open slowly for me... and again. Mm. There is a click in the left joint on opening. The muscle here is tender. I can't feel any swelling.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. That is the tender place. It is uncomfortable, though I can bear it.

[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Putting it together, the click, the pain on chewing, the grinding your partner hears and the tender muscle, and you don't feel ill. The chart says thirty-eight point three, a little warm, but there's no swelling and it isn't behaving like an abscess. My working impression is a temporomandibular joint problem driven by the grinding.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So you're not giving antibiotics? Does he need a scan?
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): No antibiotics. We might do a scan of the joint if it does not settle. I wouldn't book one today.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'd like a soft diet for a fortnight, no crusty bread, no chewing gum, and a soft mouth guard at night. The chemist will have one. It just cushions the grinding.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): A fortnight, yes. Would soup and pasta be acceptable? I shall obtain the mouth guard today, if that is suitable.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Soup, yoghurt, pasta, eggs, all fine. Steer clear of steak. Guard at night only, not in the daytime.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I should mention that work is heavy at present. I am an accountant, and it is year-end, so avoiding stress is not straightforward. I will do my best.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): The stress will keep feeding the grinding, which is why the guard matters more than another tablet. Let's see you in two weeks, and we'll go from there.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. We will return in two weeks. I am grateful for the clear explanation.
[SEG0041] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll make sure the guard actually gets worn. And no parcels of biotin from his sister.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Ha. Leave the biotin with her. If the pain suddenly blows up, or you can't open the jaw at all, come back sooner, otherwise two weeks. Mind how you go.

spec.situation: Person with jaw pain on chewing and clicking, worse with stress, teeth grinding noticed by partner; no fever; mouth guard and soft diet advice.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Tender muscle is supported; left-sided location is not stated for the muscle.
bad.text: Jaw muscle tenderness (body_site=left jaw, status=present, observed_by=doctor)

omissions.text: Patient reported no trouble with the teeth themselves.
Patient stated he can open the jaw fully; it merely clicks.
Patient takes nothing else regularly besides paracetamol.
Family member said patient's sister takes high-strength biotin for her hair and wants him to take it; patient said he has not taken the biotin and would not start it without advice.
Doctor specified the mouth guard should be worn at night only, not in the daytime.
